text.p: Malaysia on Friday closed its oldest prison, moving inmates to a new high-tech correctional facility outside Kuala Lumpur, the national Bernama news agency reported.

The closing of the 101-year-old Pudu Prison, which has held and hanged some of the most hard-core convicts, was marked by a parade, the lowering of the prison's flag and playing of the Last Post, a military funeral dirge.
The 10-hectare Pudu Prison was located on the same road as some of Kuala Lumpur's most luxurious hotels and shopping malls.
Prison authorities said the location was no longer suitable and made it difficult for them to act to stop a prison break-out.
About 1,580 prisoners were moved out between Thursday and early Friday to the 48-hectare Sungai Buloh prison, which officials said could accommodate 2,500 inmates.
The early morning operation was done to avoid traffic jams, and for security reasons, said Omar Mohamad Dan, the deputy director-general of prisons.
The government has not yet announced what will become of the facility.
The new prison is 20 miles from Kuala Lumpur. The New Straits Times newspaper reported that the prison has hidden cameras and motion detectors.
"While it is the most humane correctional facility in the country, it will also be the toughest, designed from the ground up to minimise manpower and maximise technology," the newspaper said.
